title.raw: 卷二十一 列傳第十五: 謝哲 蕭乾 謝嘏 張種 王固 孔奐 蕭允 Volume 21: Xie Zhe; Xiao Qian; Wang Gu; Kong Huan; Xiao Yun

sentences.zh: 陳書卷二十一

translations.literal: Book of Chen, Volume 21
translations.idiomatic: Book of Chen, Volume 21

sentences.zh: 列傳第十五

translations.literal: Biographies, Number Fifteen
translations.idiomatic: Biographies, Part Fifteen

sentences.zh: 謝哲 蕭乾 謝嘏 張種 王固 孔奐 蕭允弟引

translations.literal: Xie Zhe; Xiao Gan; Xie Geng; Zhang Zhong; Wang Gu; Kong Huan; Xiao Yun, with his younger brother Yin cited
translations.idiomatic: Xie Zhe; Xiao Gan; Xie Geng; Zhang Zhong; Wang Gu; Kong Huan; Xiao Yun, with his younger brother Yin cited

sentences.zh: 謝哲字穎豫，陳郡陽夏人也。

translations.literal: Xie Zhe, styled Yingyu, was a native of Yangxia in Chen commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Zhe, styled Yingyu, came from Yangxia in Chen commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖朏，梁司徒。

translations.literal: His grandfather Tian was Minister of Works of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Tian had been Liang's minister of works.

sentences.zh: 父譓，梁右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His father Yue was Right Grandee with the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yue was a right grandee with the gold seal and purple ribbon under Liang.

sentences.zh: 哲美風儀，舉止醞藉，而襟情豁然，為士君子所重。

translations.literal: Zhe was handsome in bearing, refined and easy in deportment, yet open and clear in temperament; gentlemen esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhe was handsome and graceful in manner, with a temperament open and clear; men of worth held him in esteem.

sentences.zh: 起家梁祕書郎，累遷廣陵太守。

translations.literal: He began his career as Secretariat Gentleman of Liang and rose through successive posts to Administrator of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as a secretariat gentleman of Liang and rose step by step to administrator of Guangling.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，以母老因寓居廣陵，高祖自京口渡江應接郭元建，哲乃委質，深被敬重。

translations.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion, because his mother was aged he lodged at Guangling; when the Founder crossed the river from Jingkou to link up with Guo Yuanjian, Zhe then pledged his allegiance and was deeply respected.
translations.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion his mother was old, so he stayed at Guangling. When the Founder crossed from Jingkou to join Guo Yuanjian, Zhe pledged himself to him and won deep regard.

sentences.zh: 高祖為〔南〕徐州刺史，[1]表哲為長史。

translations.literal: When the Founder was Governor of [Southern] Xuzhou, Editorial footnote marker 1. he memorialized Zhe as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder was governor of Southern Xuzhou,[1] he memorialized Zhe as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 荊州陷，高祖使哲奉表於晉安王勸進。

translations.literal: When Jingzhou fell, the Founder sent Zhe to present a memorial to the Prince of Jin'an urging accession.
translations.idiomatic: After Jingzhou fell, the Founder sent Zhe to the Prince of Jin'an with a memorial urging him to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 敬帝承制徵為給事黃門侍郎，領步兵校尉。

translations.literal: Emperor Jing, acting on the regency, summoned him as Supervising Attendant in the Yellow Gate and concurrently Colonel of Foot Soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing, exercising the regency, summoned him as supervising attendant in the Yellow Gate and made him colonel of foot soldiers as well.

sentences.zh: 貞陽侯僭位，以哲為通直散騎常侍，侍東宮。

translations.literal: When the Marquis of Zhenyang usurped the throne, he made Zhe Regular Attendant of the Direct and Upright Scattered Cavalry and attendant to the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the Marquis of Zhenyang seized the throne, he named Zhe regular attendant of the direct and upright scattered cavalry and attendant to the eastern palace.

sentences.zh: 敬帝即位，遷長兼侍中。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jing took the throne, he was promoted to chief clerk concurrent with palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jing succeeded, Zhe was promoted to chief clerk with concurrent appointment as palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 高祖受命，遷都官尚書、豫州大中正、吏部尚書。

translations.literal: When the Founder received the Mandate, Zhe was transferred to Minister of the Masters of Writing for Revenue, metropolitan governor of Yuzhou, and Minister of the Masters of Writing for Officials.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder took the Mandate, Zhe became minister of the masters of writing for revenue, metropolitan governor of Yuzhou, and minister of the masters of writing for officials.

sentences.zh: 出為明威將軍、晉陵太守，入為中書令。

translations.literal: He went out as Clear Martial General and Administrator of Jinling; he entered court as Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as clear martial general and administrator of Jinling, then returned to court as director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 世祖嗣位，為太子詹事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen succeeded, he was made Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen succeeded, he was made mentor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 出為明威將軍、衡陽內史，秩中二千石。

translations.literal: He went out as Clear Martial General and Interior Administrator of Hengyang, with salary of middle two thousand dan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as clear martial general and interior administrator of Hengyang, with salary of middle two thousand dan.

sentences.zh: 遷長沙太守，將軍、加秩如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Administrator of Changsha; his generalship and augmented salary remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to administrator of Changsha, keeping his general's title and augmented salary unchanged.

sentences.zh: 還除散騎常侍、中書令。

translations.literal: On returning he was appointed Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he was made regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 廢帝即位，以本官領前將軍。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne, he held his former posts and additionally led the Vanguard General.
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor succeeded, Zhe kept his offices and was also made to lead the vanguard general.

sentences.zh: 高宗為錄尚書，引為侍中、仁威將軍、司徒左長史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan was overseer of the masters of writing, he drew Zhe in as palace attendant, Humane Martial General, and chief clerk on the left of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan oversaw the masters of writing, he brought Zhe in as palace attendant, humane martial general, and left chief clerk to the minister of works.

sentences.zh: 未拜，光大元年卒，時年五十九。

translations.literal: Before he could take up the appointment, he died in the first year of Guangda, aged fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Guangda year 1 (567) before he could assume the post, at the age of fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中、中書監，謚康子。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given palace attendant and Director of the Secretariat in oversight, with posthumous title Kangzi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made palace attendant and overseer of the secretariat, with the posthumous title Kangzi.

sentences.zh: 蕭乾字思惕，蘭陵人也。

translations.literal: Xiao Gan, styled Siti, was a native of Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Gan, styled Siti, came from Lanling.

sentences.zh: 祖嶷，齊丞相豫章文獻王。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yi was Chancellor of Qi and Prince Wenxian of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yi was chancellor of Qi and Prince Wenxian of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 父子範，梁祕書監。

translations.literal: His father Zifan was Director of the Secretariat of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zifan was director of the secretariat under Liang.

sentences.zh: 乾容止雅正，性恬簡，善隸書，得叔父子雲之法。

translations.literal: Gan's bearing was elegant and correct, his nature quiet and spare; he excelled at clerical script and obtained the method of his uncle's son Ziyun.
translations.idiomatic: Gan was elegant and correct in deportment, quiet and spare by nature. He excelled at clerical script and mastered the hand of his cousin Ziyun.

sentences.zh: 年九歲，召補國子周易生，梁司空袁昂時為祭酒，深敬重之。

translations.literal: At nine sui he was summoned to fill a vacancy as National University student in the Zhou Changes; Yuan Ang of Liang, then Director of the National University as Minister of Works, deeply respected him.
translations.idiomatic: At nine he was called to fill a vacancy as a National University student in the Zhou Changes. Yuan Ang of Liang, then director of the university in his capacity as minister of works, held him in deep regard.

sentences.zh: 十五，舉明經。

translations.literal: At fifteen he passed the classics licentiate examination.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen he passed the classics licentiate examination.

sentences.zh: 釋褐東中郎湘東王法曹參軍，遷太子舍人。

translations.literal: He doffed the commoner's garb as aide in the law office on the staff of the Eastern Headquarters of the Prince of Xiangdong, and was promoted to Attendant in the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: He left common status as law-office aide on the Prince of Xiangdong's eastern headquarters staff, then rose to attendant in the heir apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 建安侯蕭正立出鎮南豫州，又板錄事參軍。

translations.literal: When the Marquis of Jian'an, Xiao Zhengli, went out to garrison South Yuzhou, Gan was again commissioned as recording secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When the Marquis of Jian'an, Xiao Zhengli, took up his post in South Yuzhou, Gan was again commissioned recording secretary.

sentences.zh: 累遷中軍宣城王中錄事諮議參軍。

translations.literal: He rose through successive posts to central recording secretary and advisory aide on the staff of the Prince of Xuancheng in the Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to central recording secretary and advisory aide on the Prince of Xuancheng's staff in the central army.

sentences.zh: 侯景平，高祖鎮南徐州，引乾為貞威將軍、司空從事中郎。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing was pacified, the Founder garrisoned South Xuzhou and drew Gan in as Trustworthy Martial General and attendant gentleman on the Minister of Works staff.
translations.idiomatic: After Hou Jing fell, the Founder held South Xuzhou and brought Gan in as trustworthy martial general and attendant gentleman on the minister of works staff.

sentences.zh: 遷中書侍郎、太子家令。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Secretariat Gentleman and Director of the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to secretariat gentleman and director of the heir apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 謝嘏字含茂，陳郡陽夏人也。

translations.literal: Xie Geng, styled Hanmao, was a native of Yangxia in Chen commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Geng, styled Hanmao, came from Yangxia in Chen commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖瀹，齊金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yao was Grandee with the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yao was a grandee with the gold seal and purple ribbon under Qi.

sentences.zh: 父舉，梁中衛將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: His father Ju was Central Guard General and General with the Staff Equal in Ceremony to the Three Excellencies of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ju was central guard general and a general with staff equal in ceremony to the three excellencies under Liang.

sentences.zh: 二子儼、

translations.literal: His two sons were Yan and
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons, Yan and

translations.literal: Collation variant: shen (for Zhou).
translations.idiomatic: (shen)

translations.literal: Adopted reading: Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou.

sentences.zh: [3]儼官至散騎常侍、侍中、御史中丞、太常卿，出監東揚州。

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 3. Yan reached the posts of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, palace attendant, censor-in-chief, and Minister of Ceremonies, and went out as overseer of East Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: [3] Yan rose to regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, palace attendant, censor-in-chief, and minister of ceremonies, and went out as overseer of East Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 禎明二年卒於會稽，贈中護軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenming he died at Kuaiji and was posthumously given Central Guardian General.
translations.idiomatic: He died at Kuaiji in Zhenming year 2 (583) and was posthumously made central guardian general.

sentences.zh: 張種字士苗，吳郡人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhong, styled Shimiao, was a native of Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhong, styled Shimiao, came from Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖辯，宋司空右長史、廣州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Bian was Right Chief Clerk to the Minister of Works of Song and Administrator of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Bian was right chief clerk to Song's minister of works and administrator of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 父略，梁太子中庶子、臨海太守。

translations.literal: His father Lue was Junior Mentor in the Heir Apparent's Household of Liang and Administrator of Linhai.
translations.idiomatic: His father Lue was junior mentor in the heir apparent's household under Liang and administrator of Linhai.

sentences.zh: 種少恬靜，居處雅正，不妄交遊，傍無造請，時人為之語曰：「宋稱敷、演，梁則卷、充。

translations.literal: Zhong from youth was quiet and still, correct in dwelling and deportment, and did not make friends lightly; none pressed in upon him, and people of the time said of him: "Song praised Fu and Yan; Liang had Juan and Chong.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Zhong was quiet and still, correct in his home and bearing, and would not court company idly. No one forced his door. People said, "Song praised Fu and Yan; under Liang it was Juan and Chong.

sentences.zh: 清虛學尚，種有其風。

translations.literal: In the pure and lofty scholarly ideal, Zhong has that air.
translations.idiomatic: In the love of purity and emptiness, Zhong carries that spirit.

sentences.zh: 」仕梁王府法曹，遷外兵參軍，以父憂去職。

translations.literal: " He served in the law office of a Liang princely establishment, was promoted to external military aide, and left office on his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: " He served in a Liang prince's law office, rose to external military aide, and resigned when his father died.

sentences.zh: 服闋，為中軍宣城王府主簿。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he became chief secretary on the staff of the Prince of Xuancheng in the Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he became chief secretary on the Prince of Xuancheng's staff in the central army.

sentences.zh: 種時年四十餘，家貧，求為始豐令，入除中衛西昌侯府西曹掾。

translations.literal: Zhong was then over forty; his household was poor, and he sought the magistracy of Shifeng; he entered court and was appointed western bureau aide on the staff of the Marquis of Xichang in the Central Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong was then past forty and poor at home, so he sought the magistracy of Shifeng. He entered court as western bureau aide on the Marquis of Xichang's staff in the central guard.

sentences.zh: 時武陵王為益州刺史，重選府僚，以種為征西東曹掾，種辭以母老，抗表陳請，為有司所奏，坐黜免。

translations.literal: At the time the Prince of Wuling was Inspector of Yizhou and chose his staff with care; he made Zhong eastern bureau aide on the campaign-west staff, but Zhong declined on the ground that his mother was aged, submitted a memorial in protest, was impeached by the relevant offices, and was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Wuling was then inspector of Yizhou and chose his staff carefully. He named Zhong eastern bureau aide on the campaign-west staff, but Zhong pleaded an aged mother, protested in a memorial, was impeached, and was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，種奉其母東奔，久之得達鄉里。

translations.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion Zhong escorted his mother east in flight; after a long time he reached his native district.
translations.idiomatic: In Hou Jing's rebellion Zhong fled east with his mother and only after long hardship reached home.

sentences.zh: 俄而母卒，種時年五十，而毀瘠過甚，又迫以凶荒，未獲時葬，服制雖畢，而居處飲食，恆若在喪。

translations.literal: Soon his mother died. Zhong was then fifty, yet his grief had wasted him beyond measure; moreover famine pressed him, and he could not bury her in season. Though the mourning term was complete, in dwelling and in food and drink he was always as if still in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: His mother soon died. Zhong was fifty, wasted beyond measure by grief, and famine kept him from a timely burial. When the mourning term ended, he still ate and lived as though the coffin had not left the house.

sentences.zh: 及景平，司徒王僧辯以狀

translations.literal: When Jing was pacified, Minister of Works Wang Sengbian reported the situation
translations.idiomatic: After Jing fell, Minister of Works Wang Sengbian reported the facts

translations.literal: Collation variant: present (feng).
translations.idiomatic: (present)

sentences.zh: 〔奏〕聞，[4]起為貞威將軍、治中從事史，并為具葬禮，葬訖，種方即吉。

translations.literal: Adopted reading: memorialized to the throne, Editorial footnote marker 4. and appointed him Trustworthy Martial General and Directing Secretary; he also provided the full funeral rites, and only when the burial was finished did Zhong put off mourning garb.
translations.idiomatic: and memorialized to the throne.[4] Zhong was raised to trustworthy martial general and directing secretary. Sengbian also furnished the full funeral. Only when the burial was done did Zhong lay mourning aside.

sentences.zh: 僧辯又以種年老，傍無胤嗣，賜之以妾，及居處之具。

translations.literal: Sengbian also, because Zhong was aged and had no heir at his side, bestowed a concubine on him together with household furnishings.
translations.idiomatic: Because Zhong was old and childless, Sengbian also gave him a concubine and furnishings for his home.

sentences.zh: 種沈深虛靜，而識量宏博，時人皆以為宰相之器。

translations.literal: Zhong was deep, still, and empty within, yet his discernment and capacity were vast; men of the time all regarded him as material for a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong was deep, still, and inwardly empty, yet his judgment and reach were broad. All who knew him took him for a future chief minister.

sentences.zh: 僕射徐陵嘗抗表讓位於種曰：「臣種器懷沈密，文史優裕，東南貴秀，朝庭親賢，克壯其猷，宜居左執。

translations.literal: Vice Director Xu Ling once submitted a memorial yielding his place to Zhong, saying: "Your servant Zhong's talent is deep and close-woven, his letters and histories abundant; a noble shoot of the southeast, a kinsman in talent whom the court cherishes—he can strengthen its plans and rightly should hold the left hand.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Xu Ling once memorialized to yield his seat to Zhong: "Zhong's gifts are deep and close-held, his command of letters and histories ample. He is a fine scion of the southeast and a man the court should cherish. He can fortify the state's designs and rightly should hold the left hand.

sentences.zh: 」其為時所推重如此。

translations.literal: " Such was the weight in which his age held him.
translations.idiomatic: " Such was the esteem in which his age held him.

sentences.zh: 太建五年卒，時年七十，贈特進，諡曰元子。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taijian he died, aged seventy; posthumously he was given Special Advancement, with posthumous title Yuanzi.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Taijian year 5 (573), aged seventy, and was posthumously made special advancement with the title Yuanzi.

sentences.zh: 種仁恕寡欲，雖歷居顯位，而家產屢空，終日晏然，不以為病。

translations.literal: Zhong was humane, forgiving, and of few desires; though he long held eminent posts, his household goods were repeatedly empty, yet all day he was at ease and did not count it a hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong was humane, forgiving, and wanting little. Though he long held high office, his house was often bare, yet he remained easy all day and did not call it hardship.

sentences.zh: 太建初，女為始興王妃，以居處僻陋，特賜宅一區，又累賜無錫、嘉興縣侯秩。

translations.literal: Early in Taijian his daughter became consort to the Prince of Shixing; because her dwelling was mean and remote, she was specially granted one residence, and repeatedly granted the stipend of a county marquis of Wuxi and Jiaxing.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taijian his daughter married the Prince of Shixing. Because her quarters were poor and remote, the court granted her a house and repeatedly gave her a county marquis's stipend from Wuxi and Jiaxing.

sentences.zh: [5]嘗於無錫見有重囚在獄，天寒，呼出曝日，遂失之，世祖大笑，而不深責。

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 5. Once at Wuxi he saw a heavily fettered prisoner in jail; the weather was cold, and he called him out to sun himself, whereupon the man escaped. Emperor Wen laughed greatly and did not punish him severely.
translations.idiomatic: [5] Once at Wuxi he saw a heavily shackled prisoner in jail. The day was cold, and he had the man brought out to warm in the sun; the prisoner escaped. Emperor Wen laughed and did not punish him harshly.

sentences.zh: 有集十四卷。

translations.literal: He left a collected works in fourteen juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left collected works in fourteen juan.

sentences.zh: 種弟稜，亦清靜有識度，官至司徒左長史，太建十一年卒，時年七十，贈光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Zhong's younger brother Ling was likewise quiet and possessed discernment; he reached chief clerk on the left of the Minister of Works, died in the eleventh year of Taijian aged seventy, and was posthumously given Grandee with the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong's younger brother Ling was likewise still and discerning. He rose to left chief clerk to the minister of works, died in Taijian year 11 (579) at seventy, and was posthumously made grandee with the gold seal and purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 種族子稚才，齊護軍

translations.literal: Zhong's clansman Zhi Cai; of Qi Protector-General
translations.idiomatic: Zhong's clansman Zhi Cai was grandson of

translations.literal: Collation variant: grandson (sun).
translations.idiomatic: (grandson)

sentences.zh: 沖之〔孫〕。

translations.literal: Sun Chongzhi's [grandson].
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chongzhi, protector-general of Qi.

sentences.zh: [6]少孤介特立，仕為尚書金部郎中。

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 6. From youth he was orphaned, independent, and upright; he served as Director of the Gold Bureau in the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: [6] Orphaned early, he stood alone and upright. He served as director of the gold bureau in the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 遷右丞，建康令、太舟卿、[7]揚州別駕從事史，兼散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Assistant Director, Magistrate of Jiankang, Commissioner of the Grand Fleet, Editorial footnote marker 7. and Directing Attendant of Yangzhou, concurrently Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to right assistant director, magistrate of Jiankang, commissioner of the grand fleet,[7] directing attendant of Yangzhou, and concurrent regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 使于周，還為司農、廷尉卿。

translations.literal: Sent on mission to Zhou, on return he was made Minister of Agriculture and Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Sent on embassy to Zhou, he returned to be minister of agriculture and minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 所歷並以清白稱。

translations.literal: In every post he was known for purity and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Every office he held won him a name for clean conduct.

sentences.zh: 廢帝即位，授侍中、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne, he was appointed palace attendant and Grandee with the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor succeeded, he was made palace attendant and grandee with the gold seal and purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 時高宗輔政，固以廢帝外戚，妳媼恆往來禁中，頗宣密旨，事洩，比將伏誅，[8]高宗以固本無兵權，且居處清潔，止免所居官，禁錮。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Xuan was assisting in government; because Gu was a maternal kinsman of the Deposed Emperor, wet nurses constantly came and went within the forbidden quarters and often conveyed secret orders. When the affair leaked out they were on the verge of execution, Editorial footnote marker 8. but Emperor Xuan, considering that Gu by nature had no military power and his dwelling and conduct were pure, only removed him from his posts and placed him under house arrest.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan was then regent. Gu, as the Deposed Emperor's kin by marriage, had wet nurses passing in and out of the inner palace who often carried secret orders. When the plot came out they were nearly executed,[8] but Emperor Xuan judged that Gu had no troops at his back and lived cleanly, so he only stripped his offices and confined him.

sentences.zh: 太建二年，隨例為招遠將軍、宣惠豫章王諮議參軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taijian, following precedent, he was made Inviting-from-Afar General and advisory aide on the staff of the Prince of Yuzhang, Xuanhui.
translations.idiomatic: In Taijian year 2 (574), by the usual rule, he was made inviting-from-afar general and advisory aide to the Prince of Yuzhang, Xuanhui.

sentences.zh: 遷太中大夫、太常卿、南徐州大中正。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Grand Master of the Palace, Minister of Ceremonies, and metropolitan governor of South Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to grand master of the palace, minister of ceremonies, and metropolitan governor of South Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 七年，卒官，時年六十三。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he died in office, aged sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he died in office, aged sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 贈金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given Grandee with the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made grandee with the gold seal and purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 喪事所須，隨由資給。

translations.literal: Whatever the funeral required was supplied as the occasion arose.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever the funeral required was furnished as need arose.

sentences.zh: 至德二年改葬，謚曰恭子。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhide his burial was changed, with posthumous title Gongzi.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhide year 2 (584) he was reburied and given the posthumous title Gongzi.

sentences.zh: 固清虛寡欲，居喪以孝聞。

translations.literal: Gu was pure, empty, and of few desires, and was famed for filial piety in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Gu was pure, spare, and wanting little, and won fame for filial mourning.

sentences.zh: 又崇信佛法，及丁所生母憂，遂終身蔬食，夜則坐禪，晝誦佛經，兼習成實論義，而於玄言非所長。

translations.literal: He also devoutly believed in the Buddhist law; when he completed mourning for his birth mother he thereafter ate only vegetables, sat in meditation by night, recited Buddhist sutras by day, and also studied the Chengshi treatises, yet he was not skilled in Dark Learning discourse.
translations.idiomatic: He also devoutly followed the Buddhist teaching. After mourning for his birth mother he ate only vegetables for life, meditated by night, recited sutras by day, and studied the Chengshi commentarial tradition, but excelled little in Dark Learning talk.

sentences.zh: 嘗聘于西魏，因宴饗之際，請停殺一羊，羊於固前跪拜。

translations.literal: Once on embassy to Western Wei, at a feast he asked that the killing of a sheep be stopped; the sheep knelt and bowed before Gu.
translations.idiomatic: On embassy to Western Wei, at a banquet he asked that a sheep slated for slaughter be spared; the sheep knelt and bowed before him.

sentences.zh: 又宴於昆明池，魏人以南人嗜魚，大設罟網，固以佛法呪之，遂一鱗不獲。

translations.literal: Again at a feast at Kunming Pool the Wei people, knowing southerners love fish, set out nets on a great scale; Gu invoked the Buddhist spell over them, and not a single scale was taken.
translations.idiomatic: At another feast on Kunming Pool the Wei hosts, knowing southerners relish fish, spread great nets. Gu chanted Buddhist spells, and not one fish was caught.

sentences.zh: 子寬，官至司徒左長史、侍中。

translations.literal: His son Kuan reached chief clerk on the left of the Minister of Works and palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kuan rose to left chief clerk to the minister of works and palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 孔奐字休文，會稽山陰人也。

translations.literal: Kong Huan, styled Xiuwen, was a native of Shanyin in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Huan, styled Xiuwen, came from Shanyin in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 曾祖琇之，齊左民尚書、吳興太守。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Xiuzhi was Left Minister of the People of Qi and Administrator of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Xiuzhi was left minister of the people under Qi and administrator of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 祖臶，太子舍人、尚書三公郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Tai was Attendant in the Heir Apparent's Household and Gentleman in the Three Excellencies Bureau of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Tai was attendant in the heir apparent's household and gentleman in the three excellencies bureau of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 父稚孫，梁寧遠枝江公主簿、無錫令。

translations.literal: His father Zhisun was Registrar to the Princess of Zhijiang, Branch of Ningyuan, of Liang, and Magistrate of Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhisun was registrar to the Princess of Zhijiang, branch of Ningyuan, under Liang, and magistrate of Wuxi.

sentences.zh: 奐數歲而孤，為叔父虔孫所養。

translations.literal: Huan was orphaned at several sui and was reared by his uncle Qiansun.
translations.idiomatic: Huan lost his father when he was only a few years old and was raised by his uncle Qiansun.

sentences.zh: 好學，善屬文，經史百家，莫不通涉。

translations.literal: He loved learning and was skilled at composition; the classics, histories, and the hundred schools—none did he fail to traverse.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning and wrote well. Classics, histories, and the hundred schools alike lay open to him.

sentences.zh: 沛國劉顯時稱學府，每共奐討論，深相歎服，乃執奐手曰：「 昔伯喈墳素悉與仲宣，吾當希彼蔡君，足下無愧王氏。

translations.literal: Liu Xian of Pei, then called a storehouse of learning, whenever discussed with Huan would deeply admire him; he took Huan's hand and said: "In old days Cai Yong's tomb texts all went to Wang Can; I shall hope to match that Lord Cai—you need not fall short of the Wang clan."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xian of Pei, then hailed as a treasury of learning, debated with Huan and came away deeply impressed. He took Huan's hand and said, "Once Cai Yong's tomb classics all passed to Wang Can. I would match that Lord Cai; you need not blush before the Wang house."

sentences.zh: 」所保書籍，尋以相付。

translations.literal: The books he had kept in trust he soon handed over to him.
translations.idiomatic: The books he had held in trust he soon entrusted to Huan.

sentences.zh: 州舉秀才，射策高第。

translations.literal: The province nominated him as Outstanding Talent; in the archery-and-writing examination he placed high.
translations.idiomatic: The province nominated him as outstanding talent, and he placed high in the archery-and-writing examination.

sentences.zh: 起家揚州主簿、宣惠湘東王行參軍，並不就。

translations.literal: He began his career as chief secretary of Yangzhou and mobile aide on the staff of the Prince of Xuanhui of Xiangdong, but declined both appointments.
translations.idiomatic: He was first named chief secretary of Yangzhou and mobile aide on the Prince of Xuanhui of Xiangdong's staff, but refused both posts.

sentences.zh: 又除鎮西湘東王外兵參軍，入為尚書倉部郎中，遷儀曹侍郎。

translations.literal: He was again appointed external military aide on the staff of the Prince of Xiangdong in the Campaign-West headquarters, entered court as Director of the Granary Bureau in the Masters of Writing, and was promoted to Gentleman in the Ceremonies Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was again named external military aide on the campaign-west staff of the Prince of Xiangdong, entered court as director of the granary bureau, and rose to gentleman in the ceremonies bureau.

sentences.zh: 時左民郎沈炯為飛書所謗，將陷重辟，事連臺閣，人懷憂懼，奐廷議理之，竟得明白。

translations.literal: At the time the Left Minister of the People Gentleman Shen Jiong was slandered by a flying petition and was about to fall into a capital offense; the affair touched the terrace offices, and men were fearful; Huan argued the case in court and at last secured his exoneration.
translations.idiomatic: When the left minister of the people, Gentleman Shen Jiong, was attacked by an anonymous memorial and faced a capital charge, the affair implicated the terrace offices and everyone was afraid. Huan argued the case in open court and at last cleared him.

sentences.zh: 丹陽尹何敬容以奐剛正，請補功曹史。

translations.literal: He Jingrong, Metropolitan Governor of Danyang, because Huan was upright and firm, asked that he be appointed merit officer.
translations.idiomatic: He Jingrong, metropolitan governor of Danyang, finding Huan upright and firm, asked to have him made merit officer.

sentences.zh: 出為南昌侯相，值侯景亂，不之官。

translations.literal: He went out as Chancellor of the Marquis of Nanchang but, meeting Hou Jing's rebellion, did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as chancellor to the Marquis of Nanchang, but when Hou Jing rebelled he never took up the office.

sentences.zh: 京城陷，朝士並被拘縶，或薦奐於賊帥侯子鑒，子鑒命脫桎梏，厚遇之，令掌書記。

translations.literal: When the capital fell, court gentlemen were all seized and bound; someone recommended Huan to the rebel commander Hou Zijian. Zijian ordered his fetters removed, treated him generously, and put him in charge of secretarial records.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell, court gentlemen were seized; someone recommended Huan to the rebel commander Hou Zijian. Zijian had his bonds removed, treated him well, and made him keep the secretarial records.

sentences.zh: 時景軍士悉恣其凶威，子鑒景之腹心，委任又重，朝士見者，莫不卑俯屈折，奐獨敖然自若，無所下。

translations.literal: At that time Jing's soldiers all indulged their brutal power; Zijian was Jing's trusted inner man, and his commission was weighty. Court gentlemen who saw him all bowed low and bent themselves; Huan alone was proudly at ease and would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's soldiers ran riot; Zijian, his trusted confidant, held heavy authority. Every court gentleman who met him bowed and cringed; Huan alone stood proudly at ease and would not yield.

sentences.zh: 或諫奐曰：「 當今亂世，人思苟免，獯羯無知，豈可抗之以義？

translations.literal: Someone admonished Huan, saying: "In today's chaotic age, everyone seeks merely to escape with life; the barbarian foe is ignorant—how can one oppose them with righteousness?
translations.idiomatic: Someone warned Huan: "In this chaotic age everyone only wants to survive; the barbarians know no right—how can you resist them with principle?

sentences.zh: 」奐曰：「吾性命有在，雖未能死，豈可取媚凶醜，以求全乎？

translations.literal: " Huan said: "My life and death are already settled; though I may not yet die, how could I fawn on vicious ugliness to preserve myself?
translations.idiomatic: " Huan said, "My life is already in fate's hands; though I may not die yet, how could I flatter vicious men to save myself?

sentences.zh: 」時賊徒剝掠子女，拘逼士庶，奐每保持之，得全濟者甚眾。

translations.literal: " At that time the rebels plundered children and pressed gentlemen and commoners; Huan each time protected them, and very many were wholly saved.
translations.idiomatic: " The rebels looted families and pressed the gentry; Huan shielded them again and again, and a great many were saved.

sentences.zh: 尋遭母憂，哀毀過禮。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he suffered his mother's mourning and grieved beyond the rites.
translations.idiomatic: He soon lost his mother and mourned beyond what the rites allowed.

sentences.zh: 時天下喪亂，皆不能終三年之喪，唯奐及吳國張種，在寇亂中守持法度，並以孝聞。

translations.literal: At that time all under Heaven was in mourning and chaos, and none could complete the three-year mourning; only Huan and Zhang Zhong of Wu commandery, amid bandit turmoil, upheld the law and were both famed for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was in chaos and almost no one could keep three-year mourning; only Huan and Zhang Zhong of Wu, amid the raids, held to the rites and won a name for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 高祖作相，除司徒右長史，遷給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: When the Founder served as Chancellor, Huan was made Right Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education and promoted to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate for Presenting Matters.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder was chancellor, Huan became right chief clerk of the minister of education, then attendant gentleman of the Yellow Gate for presenting matters.

sentences.zh: 齊遣東方老、蕭軌等來寇，軍至後湖，都邑搔擾，又四方壅隔，糧運不繼，三軍取給，唯在京師，乃除奐為貞威將軍、建康令。

translations.literal: Qi sent Dongfang Lao, Xiao Gui, and others to raid; the army reached Rear Lake, the capital was in uproar, and on all sides communications were cut so grain transport could not continue. The three armies drew supplies only from the capital region; Huan was then made Zhenwei General and Magistrate of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Qi sent Dongfang Lao, Xiao Gui, and others to invade. Their army reached Rear Lake, the capital was in turmoil, and supplies from every quarter were cut off. The armies fed only from the capital region, so Huan was made zhenwei general and magistrate of Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 時累歲兵荒，戶口流散，勍敵忽至，徵求無所，高祖剋日決戰，乃令奐多營麥飯，以荷葉裹之，一宿之閒，得數萬裹，軍人旦食訖，棄其餘，因而決戰，遂大破賊。

translations.literal: For years there had been war and famine, households had scattered, and a strong foe had suddenly arrived; levies could be found nowhere. The Founder set a day for decisive battle and ordered Huan to prepare many portions of barley meal wrapped in lotus leaves; within one night he obtained tens of thousands of bundles. The soldiers ate their fill at dawn and threw away the rest; they then joined battle and utterly broke the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: After years of war and famine the population had scattered and a powerful enemy was at the gates, yet nothing could be levied. The Founder fixed a day for battle and had Huan prepare tens of thousands of barley-ration bundles wrapped in lotus leaves overnight. The troops ate at dawn, threw away the rest, fought, and routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，遷太子中庶子。

translations.literal: When the Founder received the Mandate, Huan was moved to Attendant of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder took the throne, Huan was made attendant of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 永定二年，除晉陵太守。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongding he was made Administrator of Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongding year 2 (558) he was made administrator of Jinling.

sentences.zh: 晉陵自宋、齊以來，舊為大郡，雖經寇擾，猶為全實，前後二千石多行侵暴，奐清白自守，妻子並不之官，唯以單船臨郡，所得秩俸，隨即分贍孤寡，郡中大悅，號曰「神君」。

translations.literal: Jinling from Song and Qi times had been a great commandery; though it had suffered raids, it was still whole and substantial. Former administrators of two thousand dan had mostly practiced oppression and violence; Huan kept himself pure and held to integrity, wife and children all did not go to office with him, and he came to the commandery in a single boat. Whatever salary he received he at once divided to succor orphans and widows; the commandery rejoiced greatly and called him the "Spirit Lord."
translations.idiomatic: Jinling had been a great commandery since Song and Qi days; though raided, it was still comparatively intact. Earlier administrators had mostly been brutal; Huan lived cleanly, left wife and children at home, and entered the commandery in one small boat. He gave his salary at once to orphans and widows, and the commandery hailed him as the Spirit Lord.

sentences.zh: 曲阿富人殷綺，見奐居處素儉，乃餉衣一襲，氈被一具。

translations.literal: Yin Qi, a rich man of Qu'e, seeing Huan's dwelling plain and spare, thereupon sent him one suit of clothes and one felt quilt.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Qi, a wealthy man of Qu'e, saw how plainly Huan lived and sent him a suit of clothes and a felt quilt.

sentences.zh: 奐曰：「太守身居美祿，何為不能辦此，但民有未周，不容獨享溫飽耳。

translations.literal: Huan said: "The Administrator enjoys a fine salary—why could he not provide these himself? But the people are not yet provided for; he cannot enjoy warmth and full belly alone.
translations.idiomatic: Huan said, "The administrator enjoys a fine salary and could easily afford these himself, but the people are not yet cared for; he cannot keep comfort to himself alone.

sentences.zh: 勞卿厚意，幸勿為煩。」

translations.literal: I thank you for your generous intent; please do not trouble yourself further."
translations.idiomatic: I thank you for your kindness; please give yourself no further trouble."

sentences.zh: 初，世祖在吳中，聞奐善政，及踐祚，徵為御史中丞，領揚州大中正。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Emperor Wen was in Wu, he heard of Huan's good governance; when he ascended the throne he summoned him as Imperial Censor-in-Chief and concurrently Grand Arbiter of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Emperor Wen was in Wu, he heard of Huan's good rule; on taking the throne he summoned him as imperial censor-in-chief and grand arbiter of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 奐性剛直，善持理，多所糾劾，朝廷甚敬憚之。

translations.literal: Huan's nature was stern and upright; he was skilled at holding to principle and impeached many; the court greatly respected and feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Huan was stern and upright, skilled at principle, and impeached many; the court respected and feared him.

sentences.zh: 深達治體，每所敷奏，上未嘗不稱善，百司滯事，皆付奐決之。

translations.literal: Deeply penetrating the body of governance, whenever he presented memorials the sovereign never failed to praise them; stalled business of the hundred offices was all entrusted to Huan for decision.
translations.idiomatic: He understood governance deeply; the emperor always praised his memorials, and stalled business of every office was sent to Huan for decision.

sentences.zh: 遷散騎常侍，領步兵校尉，中書舍人，掌詔誥，揚、東揚二州大中正。

translations.literal: He was moved to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, concurrently Colonel of the Footsoldiers, Secretariat Drafter, in charge of edicts and proclamations, and Grand Arbiter of Yang and East Yang provinces.
translations.idiomatic: He was made regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, colonel of the footsoldiers, secretariat drafter in charge of edicts, and grand arbiter of Yang and East Yang.

sentences.zh: 天嘉四年，重除御史中丞，尋為五兵尚書，常侍、中正如故。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianjia he was again made Imperial Censor-in-Chief; soon he became Minister of the Five Armies, regular attendant and grand arbiter unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjia year 4 (563) he was again imperial censor-in-chief, then minister of the five armies while keeping his attendant and arbiter posts.

sentences.zh: 時世祖不豫，臺閣眾事，並令僕射到仲舉共奐決之。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Wen was unwell; all affairs of the Secretariat were ordered decided jointly by Vice Director Dao Zhongju and Huan.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen fell ill, all secretariat business was entrusted to Vice Director Dao Zhongju and Huan together.

sentences.zh: 及世祖疾篤，奐與高宗及仲舉并吏部尚書袁樞、中書舍人劉師知等入侍醫藥。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen's illness grew grave, Huan with Emperor Xuan and Zhongju, together with Minister of Personnel Yuan Shu, Secretariat Drafter Liu Shizhi, and others entered to attend medicine.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen grew critically ill, Huan entered with Emperor Xuan, Zhongju, Yuan Shu, minister of personnel, Liu Shizhi, secretariat drafter, and others to tend his medicine.

sentences.zh: 世祖嘗謂奐等曰：「今三方鼎峙，生民未乂，四海事重，宜須長君。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen once said to Huan and the rest: "Today the three realms stand like a tripod; the living people are not yet settled; the affairs of the four seas are weighty and require a mature ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen once told Huan and the others, "The three realms stand divided; the people are not yet at peace; the empire needs a mature ruler.

sentences.zh: 朕欲近則晉成，遠隆殷法，卿等須遵此意。

translations.literal: I wish, near at hand, to follow Jin's Emperor Cheng, and far off to exalt the law of the Yin dynasty—you must follow this intent.
translations.idiomatic: I mean, in the near case to follow Jin Emperor Cheng, and in the distant case to exalt Yin succession law—you must heed this intent.

sentences.zh: 」奐乃流涕歔欷而對曰：「陛下御膳違和，痊復非久，皇太子春秋鼎盛，聖德日躋，安成王介弟之尊，足為周旦，阿衡宰輔，若有廢立之心，臣等愚誠，不敢聞詔。

translations.literal: " Huan then, weeping and sobbing, answered: "Your Majesty's imperial meal is out of harmony; recovery is not far off. The crown prince is in the prime of youth, his sagely virtue daily ascending. The Prince of Ancheng enjoys the honor of a younger brother and is fully fit to be the Duke of Zhou, Yi Yin as assisting minister. If there is any thought of deposing and establishing, your servants in their foolish loyalty dare not hear such an edict.
translations.idiomatic: " Huan wept as he answered, "Your Majesty's illness is not lasting; recovery is near. The crown prince is young and full of promise. The Prince of Ancheng has a younger brother's standing and could be a Duke of Zhou, an Yi Yin at court. If anyone thinks of deposing and establishing, we in our foolish loyalty dare not hear such an order.

sentences.zh: 」世祖曰：「古之遺直，復見於卿。

translations.literal: " Emperor Wen said: "The straight remnant of antiquity—I see it again in you.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Wen said, "The straight remnant of antiquity—I see it again in you.

sentences.zh: 」天康元年，乃用奐為太子詹事，二州中正如故。

translations.literal: " In the first year of Tiankang he was then appointed Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince, the two provinces' grand arbiter unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: " In Tiankang year 1 (566) he was made grand tutor of the crown prince, retaining his grand arbiter posts in the two provinces.

sentences.zh: 世祖崩，廢帝即位，除散騎常侍、國子祭酒。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen died, the Deposed Emperor took the throne; Huan was made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Director of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen died and the Deposed Emperor succeeded, Huan was made scattered-cavalry regular attendant and director of the national university.

sentences.zh: 光大二年，出為信武將軍、南中郎康樂侯長史、尋陽太守，行江州事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangda he went out as Xinwu General, Chief Clerk to the Southern Central Commander and Marquis of Kangle, Administrator of Xunyang, and acting Governor of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangda year 2 (567) he was sent out as xinwu general, chief clerk to the southern central commander and Marquis of Kangle, administrator of Xunyang, and acting governor of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，進號仁威將軍、雲麾始興王長史，餘並如故。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan took the throne, Huan's title was advanced to Renwei General and Chief Clerk to the Cloud-Banner Prince of Shixing; the rest remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, Huan was promoted to renwei general and chief clerk to the cloud-banner Prince of Shixing; the rest of his posts stayed the same.

sentences.zh: 奐在職清儉，多所規正，高宗嘉之，賜米五百斛，并累降敕書殷勤勞問。

translations.literal: Huan in office was pure and sparing; he corrected many things, and Emperor Xuan praised him, bestowing five hundred hu of grain and repeatedly sending edicts with earnest inquiries after his welfare.
translations.idiomatic: Huan served cleanly and frugally and corrected many abuses; Emperor Xuan praised him, gave five hundred hu of grain, and repeatedly sent edicts of warm inquiry.

sentences.zh: 太建三年，徵為度支尚書，領右軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taijian he was summoned as Minister of Revenue and concurrently Right Army General.
translations.idiomatic: In Taijian year 3 (571) he was recalled as minister of revenue and right army general.

sentences.zh: 五年，改領太子中庶子，與左僕射徐陵參掌尚書五條事。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was changed to Attendant of the Crown Prince and with Left Vice Director Xu Ling jointly handled the Five Articles of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he was made attendant of the crown prince and with Left Vice Director Xu Ling jointly handled the five articles of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 六年，遷吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was moved to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 he was made minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 七年，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was given the added title Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 he was given the added title scattered-cavalry regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 八年，改加侍中。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was changed to Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 he was made attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 時有事北討，剋復淮、泗，徐、豫酋長，降附相繼，封賞選敘，紛紜重疊，奐應接引進，門無停賓。

translations.literal: At that time there was a northern campaign; Huai and Si were recovered, chieftains of Xu and Yu surrendered in succession, enfeoffments and selections for office piled up in confusion, and Huan met and advanced them—his gate knew no idle guest.
translations.idiomatic: During the northern campaign, when Huai and Si were recovered and Xu and Yu chiefs surrendered one after another, rewards and appointments piled up; Huan received and advanced them, and his gate never stood empty.

sentences.zh: 加以鑒識人物，詳練百氏，凡所甄拔，衣冠縉紳，莫不悅伏。

translations.literal: Moreover he discerned men and was thoroughly versed in the hundred clans; all whom he selected among the gentry in caps and sashes submitted gladly.
translations.idiomatic: He also judged men well and knew the great families thoroughly; every gentry man he chose submitted gladly.

sentences.zh: 性耿介，絕請託，雖儲副之尊，公侯之重，溺情相及，終不為屈。

translations.literal: By nature he was unyielding and cut off all private requests; though the heir's dignity or the weight of dukes and marquises, if feeling overflowed toward him, in the end he would not bend.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was unyielding and refused all private requests; neither the heir's rank nor the weight of dukes and marquises could make him bend.

sentences.zh: 始興王叔陵之在湘州，累諷有司，固求台鉉。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Shixing, Shuling, was in Xiangzhou, he repeatedly hinted to the relevant offices and firmly sought capital ministerial posts.
translations.idiomatic: While Prince Shixing, Shuling, was in Xiangzhou, he repeatedly pressed the offices and demanded capital ministerial posts.

sentences.zh: 奐曰：「羇章之職，本以德舉，未必皇枝。

translations.literal: Huan said: "Capital memorial-review posts are by nature raised through virtue and need not be imperial kin.
translations.idiomatic: Huan said, "Capital memorial-review posts are raised by virtue and need not go to imperial kin.

sentences.zh: 」因抗言於高宗。

translations.literal: " He thereupon spoke boldly to Emperor Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: " He then spoke boldly to Emperor Xuan.

sentences.zh: 高宗曰：「始興那忽望公，且朕兒為公，須在鄱陽王後。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan said: "How could Shixing suddenly aspire to such a post? Besides, if my son were to hold it, he would have to come after the Prince of Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan said, "How could Shixing suddenly want such a post? Even if my son held it, he would rank after the Prince of Poyang.

sentences.zh: 」奐曰：「臣之所見，亦如聖旨。

translations.literal: " Huan said: "What your servant sees is also as in the sacred edict.
translations.idiomatic: " Huan said, "What I see agrees with Your Majesty's intent.

sentences.zh: 」後主時在東宮，欲以江總為太子詹事，令管記陸瑜言之於奐。

translations.literal: " Houzhu was then in the Eastern Palace and wished to make Jiang Zong Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince; he had Recorder Lu Yu speak of it to Huan.
translations.idiomatic: " Houzhu was then in the eastern palace and wanted Jiang Zong as grand tutor; he had recorder Lu Yu raise it with Huan.

sentences.zh: 奐謂瑜曰：「江有潘、陸之華，而無園、綺之實，輔弼儲宮，竊有所難。

translations.literal: Huan told Yu: "Jiang has the brilliance of Pan Yue and Lu Ji, but not the solid worth of Qiuyuan and Chaofu; to assist and support the heir's palace, I privately find it difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Huan told Yu, "Jiang has Pan Yue and Lu Ji's brilliance, but not Qiuyuan and Chaofu's solid worth; as tutor to the heir I find it hard to approve.

sentences.zh: 」瑜具以白後主，後主深以為恨，乃自言於高宗。

translations.literal: " Yu reported it fully to Houzhu; Houzhu deeply resented it and thereupon spoke of it himself to Emperor Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: " Yu reported this fully to Houzhu, who deeply resented it and then spoke to Emperor Xuan himself.

sentences.zh: 高宗將許之，奐乃奏曰：「江總文華之人，今皇太子文華不少，豈藉於總！

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan was about to assent; Huan then memorialized, saying: "Jiang Zong is a man of literary brilliance; the present crown prince already has no little literary brilliance—why rely on Zong!
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan was about to agree when Huan memorialized: "Jiang Zong is a literary man, but the crown prince already has brilliance enough—why need Zong?

sentences.zh: 如臣愚見，願選敦重之才，以居輔導。

translations.literal: In your servant's foolish view, I wish to choose a man of solid weight to occupy the post of guidance.
translations.idiomatic: In my humble view, choose a man of solid weight for the tutor's post.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「即如卿言，誰當居此？

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "If it is as you say, who should hold this?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "If that is so, who should hold it?

sentences.zh: 」奐曰：「 都官尚書王廓，世有懿德，識性敦敏，可以居之。

translations.literal: " Huan said: "Minister of Justice Wang Kuo, of a family with fine virtue through generations, knowing and by nature solid and quick, can hold it.
translations.idiomatic: " Huan said, "Wang Kuo, minister of justice, comes from a family of fine virtue and is solid and quick in judgment—he can hold it.

sentences.zh: 」後主時亦在側，乃曰：「廓王泰之子，不可居太子詹事。

translations.literal: " Houzhu was then also at the side and said: "Kuo is the son of Wang Tai—he cannot hold the post of Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: " Houzhu, who was also present, said, "Kuo is Wang Tai's son—he cannot be grand tutor.

sentences.zh: 」奐又奏曰：「宋朝范廚即范泰之子，亦為太子詹事，前代不疑。

translations.literal: " Huan again memorialized, saying: "In Liu Song, Fan Chu was the son of Fan Tai and also served as Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince; former ages did not doubt it.
translations.idiomatic: " Huan memorialized again: "Under Liu Song, Fan Chu, Fan Tai's son, was grand tutor, and earlier ages raised no objection.

sentences.zh: 」後主固爭之，帝卒以總為詹事，由是忤旨。

translations.literal: " Houzhu stubbornly disputed it; the Emperor in the end made Zong Grand Tutor, and from this Huan went against the imperial intent.
translations.idiomatic: " Houzhu argued stubbornly; the emperor finally made Zong grand tutor, and Huan fell foul of the throne.

sentences.zh: 其梗正如此。

translations.literal: His unyielding uprightness was like this.
translations.idiomatic: His unyielding character was like this.

sentences.zh: 子紹薪、紹忠。

translations.literal: His sons were Shaoxin and Shaozhong.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Shaoxin and Shaozhong.

sentences.zh: 紹忠字孝揚，亦有才學，官至太子洗馬、儀同鄱陽王東曹掾。

translations.literal: Shaozhong, styled Xiaoyang, also had talent and learning; he reached the posts of Attendant of the Crown Prince and Eastern Staff Officer to the Prince of Poyang, Equal in Rank to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Shaozhong, styled Xiaoyang, was also talented and learned; he rose to crown prince attendant and eastern staff officer to the Prince of Poyang, equal in rank to the three dukes.

sentences.zh: 蕭允字

translations.literal: Xiao Yun styled
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yun styled

translations.literal: (Sheng)
translations.idiomatic: (Sheng)

sentences.zh: 〔叔〕佐，[9]蘭陵人也。

translations.literal: [Uncle] Zuo, Editorial footnote marker 9. was a native of Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: [Uncle] Zuo [9] was from Lanling.

sentences.zh: 曾祖思話，宋征西將軍、開府儀同三司、尚書右僕射，[10]封陽穆公。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Sihua was Song Western Campaigning General, Bearer of the Staff with Equal Court Ceremony to the Three Dukes, and Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Editorial footnote marker 10. enfeoffed as Duke Yangmu.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Sihua was Song's western campaigning general, bearer of the staff with equal court ceremony to the three dukes, and right vice director of the masters of writing [10], enfeoffed as Duke Yangmu.

sentences.zh: [11]祖惠蒨，散騎常侍、太府卿、左民尚書。

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 11. His grandfather Huilian was Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Director of the Imperial Household Treasury, and Minister of the Left for the People.
translations.idiomatic: [11] His grandfather Huilian was scattered-cavalry regular attendant, director of the imperial household treasury, and minister of the left for the people.

sentences.zh: 父介。

translations.literal: His father Jie.
translations.idiomatic: His father was Jie.

sentences.zh: 梁侍中、都官尚書。

translations.literal: Liang Palace Attendant and Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liang he was palace attendant and minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 允少知名，風神凝遠，通達有識鑒，容止醞藉，動合規矩。

translations.literal: Yun was known from youth; his spirit was concentrated and far-reaching, penetrating and with discernment; his bearing was refined and restrained, his movements all fitting rule.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was known from youth for a spirit concentrated and far-reaching, penetration and discernment, refined bearing, and conduct that always fit the rules.

sentences.zh: 起家邵陵王法曹參軍，轉湘東王主簿，遷太子洗馬。

translations.literal: He began his career as Legal Clerk to the Prince of Shaoling, moved to Chief Clerk of the Prince of Xiangdong, and was promoted to Attendant of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: He began as legal clerk to the Prince of Shaoling, became chief clerk to the Prince of Xiangdong, then crown prince attendant.

sentences.zh: 侯景攻陷臺城，百僚奔散，允獨整衣冠坐于宮坊，景軍人敬而弗之逼也。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing stormed and took the Terrace City, the hundred officials fled in disorder; Yun alone straightened cap and robes and sat in the palace quarter, and Jing's soldiers respected him and did not press him.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing took the Terrace City, officials fled in disorder; Yun alone straightened his dress and sat in the palace quarter, and Jing's soldiers respected him and did not molest him.

sentences.zh: 尋出居京口。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he went out to dwell at Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: He soon moved to Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 時寇賊縱橫，百姓波駭，衣冠士族，四出奔散，允獨不行。

translations.literal: At that time bandits and rebels ran wild, the common people were tossed in waves of terror, and gentry clans fled in all directions; Yun alone did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits ran wild and the people panicked; gentry families fled in every direction, but Yun would not go.

sentences.zh: 人問其故，允答曰：「夫性命之道，自有常分，豈可逃而獲免乎？

translations.literal: When people asked the reason, Yun answered: "The way of life and death has its constant allotment—how can one flee and thereby escape?
translations.idiomatic: Asked why, Yun answered, "Life and death have their allotted share—how can fleeing bring escape?

sentences.zh: 但患難之生，皆生於利，苟不求利，禍從何生？

translations.literal: But the birth of hardship all comes from profit; if one does not seek profit, from what does calamity arise?
translations.idiomatic: Hardship always comes from chasing profit; if you do not seek profit, whence comes disaster?

sentences.zh: 方今百姓爭欲奮臂而論大功，一言而取卿相，亦何事於一書生哉？

translations.literal: Now the common people all wish to bare their arms and dispute great merit; with one word to take minister and chancellor—what business is that of one bookish man?
translations.idiomatic: Now everyone wants to fight for great merit and win minister or chancellor with a single word—what is that to a bookish man?

sentences.zh: 莊周所謂畏影避跡，吾弗為也。

translations.literal: What Zhuang Zhou called fearing one's shadow and fleeing one's footprints—I will not do it.
translations.idiomatic: What Zhuang Zhou called fearing one's shadow and fleeing one's footprints—I will not do that.

sentences.zh: 」乃閉門靜處，并日而食，卒免於患。

translations.literal: " He then shut his door and dwelt quietly, eating every other day, and in the end escaped calamity.
translations.idiomatic: " He shut his door and lived quietly, eating every other day, and in the end escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 侯景平後，高祖鎮南徐州，以書召之，允又辭疾。

translations.literal: After Hou Jing was pacified, the Founder garrisoned South Xuzhou and summoned him by letter; Yun again declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: After Hou Jing was pacified, the Founder held South Xuzhou and summoned him by letter; Yun again pleaded illness.

sentences.zh: 永定中，侯安都為南徐州刺史，躬造其廬，以申長幼之敬。

translations.literal: In the Yongding era, Hou Andu was Inspector of South Xuzhou; he came in person to his hut to express the respect due between elder and younger.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongding era Hou Andu, inspector of South Xuzhou, came in person to his hut to pay the respect due between elder and younger.

sentences.zh: 天嘉三年，徵為太子庶子。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianjia he was summoned as Attendant of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjia year 3 (562) he was summoned as crown prince attendant.

sentences.zh: [12]三年，除稜威將軍、丹陽尹丞。

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 12. In the third year he was made Lingwei General and Assistant to the Administrator of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: [12] In the third year he was made lingwei general and assistant to the administrator of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 五年，兼侍中，聘于周，還拜中書侍郎、大匠卿。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was concurrently Attendant-in-Ordinary, sent on embassy to Zhou, and on return was made Secretariat Gentleman and Director of the Great Works.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he was concurrently attendant-in-ordinary, sent as envoy to Zhou, and on return made secretariat gentleman and director of the great works.

sentences.zh: 至德三年，除中衛豫章王長史，累遷通直散騎常侍、光勝將軍、司徒左長史、安德宮少府。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhide he was made Chief Clerk to the Central Guard Prince of Yuzhang, and cumulatively moved to Direct-Communication Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Guangsheng General, Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education, and Interior Steward of the Andre Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhide year 3 (585) he was chief clerk to the central guard Prince of Yuzhang, then direct-communication regular attendant, guangsheng general, left chief clerk of the minister of education, and interior steward of the Andre Palace.

sentences.zh: 鎮衛鄱陽王出鎮會稽，允又為長史，帶會稽郡丞。

translations.literal: When the Garrisoning Prince of Poyang went out to garrison Kuaiji, Yun again served as his chief clerk and concurrently Assistant Administrator of Kuaiji commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When the garrisoning Prince of Poyang went out to hold Kuaiji, Yun again served as his chief clerk and assistant administrator of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 行經延陵季子廟，設蘋藻之薦，託為異代之交，為詩以敘意，辭理清典。

translations.literal: Passing the shrine of Lord Ji of Yanling at Yanling, he set offerings of duckweed and water-chestnut, entrusting himself as a friend across different ages, and composed a poem to express his intent—its wording clear and classical.
translations.idiomatic: Passing Lord Ji of Yanling's shrine at Yanling, he set duckweed and water-chestnut offerings, called himself a friend across ages, and wrote a poem to express it in clear, classical wording.

sentences.zh: 後主嘗問蔡徵曰：「卿世與蕭允相知，此公志操何如？

translations.literal: Houzhu once asked Cai Zheng: "You and Xiao Yun have known each other for generations—what is this gentleman's resolve and conduct like?
translations.idiomatic: Houzhu once asked Cai Zheng, "Your family has known Xiao Yun for generations—what is his resolve and conduct like?

sentences.zh: 」徵曰：「其清虛玄遠，殆不可測，至於文章，可得而言。

translations.literal: " Zheng said: "In his purity, emptiness, and remoteness he is almost beyond measure; as for his writings, one may speak of them.
translations.idiomatic: " Zheng said, "In purity and remoteness he is almost beyond measure; as for his writing, one can speak of that.

sentences.zh: 」因誦允詩以對，後主嗟賞久之。

translations.literal: " He thereupon recited Yun's poem in reply; Houzhu sighed in admiration a long while.
translations.idiomatic: " He then recited Yun's poem in answer; Houzhu admired it at length.

sentences.zh: 其年拜光祿大夫。

translations.literal: That year he was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was made grand master of splendid virtue.

sentences.zh: 及隋師濟江，允遷于關右。

translations.literal: When the Sui army crossed the Yangzi, Yun moved to the Guan region.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sui army crossed the Yangzi, Yun moved to the Guan region.

sentences.zh: 是時朝士至長安者，例並授官，唯允與尚書僕射謝伷辭以老疾，隋文帝義之，並厚賜錢帛。

translations.literal: At that time court gentlemen who reached Chang'an were by rule all given office; only Yun and Minister of the Masters of Writing Xie Gang declined on grounds of age and illness. Emperor Wen of Sui approved their conduct and richly bestowed money and silk on them both.
translations.idiomatic: Court gentlemen who reached Chang'an were usually given office; only Yun and Xie Gang, minister of the masters of writing, declined on grounds of age and illness. Emperor Wen of Sui approved and richly rewarded them both.

sentences.zh: 尋以疾卒於長安，時年八十四。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died of illness in Chang'an, aged eighty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died of illness in Chang'an, aged eighty-four.

sentences.zh: 弟引。

translations.literal: His younger brother Yin.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother was Yin.

sentences.zh: 引字

translations.literal: Yin styled
translations.idiomatic: Yin styled

translations.literal: (Sheng)
translations.idiomatic: (Sheng)

sentences.zh: 〔叔〕休。

translations.literal: [Uncle] Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: [Uncle] Xiu.

sentences.zh: [13]方正有器局，望之儼然，雖造次之間，必由法度。

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 13. Upright in conduct with breadth of presence, in bearing he was stern; even in hurried moments he always followed rule.
translations.idiomatic: [13] Upright in conduct and breadth of bearing, he looked stern; even in haste he kept to rule.

sentences.zh: 性聰敏，博學，善屬文。

translations.literal: By nature clever and keen, broadly learned, skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Clever, broadly learned, and skilled at writing.

sentences.zh: 釋褐著作佐郎，轉西昌侯儀同府主簿。

translations.literal: He doffed the commoner's garb as Editorial Assistant of Writings and moved to Chief Clerk of the Prince of Xichang, Equal in Rank to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as editorial assistant of writings, then chief clerk to the Prince of Xichang, equal in rank to the three dukes.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，梁元帝為荊州刺史，朝士多往歸之。

translations.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion, Emperor Yuan of Liang was Inspector of Jingzhou and many court gentlemen went to join him.
translations.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion, when Emperor Yuan of Liang was inspector of Jingzhou, many court gentlemen went to him.

sentences.zh: 引曰：「諸王力爭，禍患方始，今日逃難，未是擇君之秋。

translations.literal: Yin said: "The princes are all contending for power; calamity has only begun. To flee hardship today is not yet the season for choosing a lord.
translations.idiomatic: Yin said, "The princes are fighting for power; disaster has only begun. To flee today is not yet the time to choose a lord.

sentences.zh: 吾家再世為始興郡，遺愛在民，正可南行以存家門耳。

translations.literal: Our house has for two generations served as Shixing commandery; lingering care remains among the people—we may rightly go south to preserve the family line.
translations.idiomatic: Our family has held Shixing commandery for two generations, and the people still cherish us. We should go south and keep the line alive.

sentences.zh: 」於是與弟彤及宗親等百餘人奔嶺表。

translations.literal: " Thereupon together with his younger brother Tong and more than a hundred clansmen and kin he fled to the Lingnan region.
translations.idiomatic: " He then fled to Lingnan with his brother Tong and more than a hundred kinsmen.

sentences.zh: 時始興人歐陽頠為衡州刺史，引往依焉。

translations.literal: At the time Ouyang Hao of Shixing was inspector of Hengzhou; Yin went to rely on him.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Hao of Shixing was then inspector of Hengzhou, and Yin went to join him.

sentences.zh: 頠後遷為廣州，病死，子紇領其眾。

translations.literal: Hao was later transferred to Guangzhou, died of illness, and his son He took command of his following.
translations.idiomatic: Hao was later moved to Guangzhou, died there, and his son He took over his forces.

sentences.zh: 引每疑紇有異，因事規正，由是情禮漸疏。

translations.literal: Yin often suspected He of ulterior intent; because of affairs he admonished and corrected him, and from this ritual feeling gradually grew distant.
translations.idiomatic: Yin often suspected He of hidden designs and tried to correct him when occasions arose, so their courtesy grew strained.

sentences.zh: 及紇舉兵反，時京都士人岑之敬、公孫挺等並皆惶駭，唯引恬然，謂之敬等曰：「管幼安、袁曜卿亦但安坐耳。

translations.literal: When He raised troops in rebellion, the capital literati Qin Zhijing, Gongsun Ting, and others were all terrified and alarmed; only Yin was at ease, and said to Zhijing and the others: "Guan Ning and Yuan Xi too merely sat quietly.
translations.idiomatic: When He rebelled, the capital scholars Qin Zhijing, Gongsun Ting, and others were all in terror; only Yin was calm. He told Zhijing and the rest, "Guan Ning and Yuan Xi too only sat still.

sentences.zh: 君子正身以明道，直己以行義，亦復何憂懼乎？

translations.literal: The gentleman straightens the person to illuminate the Way, makes himself upright to enact righteousness—what need is there for worry and fear?
translations.idiomatic: A gentleman sets his person right to show the Way and keeps himself straight to act with righteousness—what is there to fear?

sentences.zh: 」及章昭達平番禺，引始北還。

translations.literal: " When Zhang Zhaoda pacified Panyu, Yin at last returned north.
translations.idiomatic: " After Zhang Zhaoda pacified Panyu, Yin at last came back north.

sentences.zh: 高宗召引問嶺表事，引具陳始末，帝甚悅，即日拜金部侍郎。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan summoned Yin to question him on affairs beyond the ranges; Yin stated the whole course from beginning to end; the emperor was greatly pleased and that same day invested him as vice minister of the gold office.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan summoned Yin to ask about the south. Yin laid out the whole story; the emperor was delighted and that day made him vice minister of the gold office.

sentences.zh: 引善隸書，為當時所重。

translations.literal: Yin was skilled at clerical script and was valued by his age.
translations.idiomatic: Yin excelled at clerical script and was highly regarded in his day.

sentences.zh: 高宗嘗披奏事，指引署名曰：「此字筆勢翩翩，似鳥之欲飛。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan once spread out memorials for business; pointing to Yin's signature he said: "This character's brush momentum is fluttering, like a bird about to fly.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan once went through memorials and, pointing to Yin's signature, said, "The brushwork is light and swift, like a bird about to take flight.

sentences.zh: 」引謝曰：「此乃陛下假其羽毛耳。

translations.literal: " Yin thanked him, saying: "This is Your Majesty lending it feathers.
translations.idiomatic: " Yin replied, "That is because Your Majesty lent it feathers.

sentences.zh: 」又謂引曰：「我每有所忿，見卿輒意解，何也？

translations.literal: " He also said to Yin: "Whenever I am angry, on seeing you my mind is eased—why?
translations.idiomatic: " He also asked Yin, "Whenever I am angry, seeing you calms me. Why is that?

sentences.zh: 」引曰：「此自陛下不遷怒，臣何預此恩。

translations.literal: " Yin said: "This is because Your Majesty does not shift anger; how could your servant share in this grace?
translations.idiomatic: " Yin said, "Your Majesty does not vent anger on others. How could a subject claim credit for that?

sentences.zh: 」太建七年，加戎昭將軍。

translations.literal: " In the seventh year of Taijian he was given the added rank of martial-awe general.
translations.idiomatic: " In Taijian year 7 he was given the added rank of martial-awe general.

sentences.zh: 九年，除中衛始興王諮議參軍，兼金部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was made staff adviser to the Prince of Shixing, central guard, and concurrently vice minister of the gold office.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9 he was made staff adviser to the prince of Shixing in the central guard and kept the gold-office vice ministry.

sentences.zh: 引性抗直，不事權貴，左右近臣，無所造請，高宗每欲遷用，輒為用事者所裁。

translations.literal: Yin's nature was upright and unyielding; he did not serve the powerful; to close attendants at court he made no visits of request; whenever Emperor Xuan wished to promote him, he was at once cut short by those in power.
translations.idiomatic: Yin was upright and would not court the powerful; he never paid calls on the emperor's intimates. Whenever Emperor Xuan meant to advance him, the men in power blocked it.

sentences.zh: 及呂梁覆師，戎儲空匱，乃轉引為庫部侍郎，掌知營造弓弩槊箭等事。

translations.literal: When the army was destroyed at Lülü Mountain and military stores stood empty, he was transferred to vice minister of the storehouse office, in charge of manufacturing bows, crossbows, spears, arrows, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: After the disaster at Lülü Mountain left the arsenals bare, he was moved to vice minister of the storehouse office to oversee the making of bows, crossbows, spears, and arrows.

sentences.zh: 引在職一年，而器械充牣。

translations.literal: Yin held office one year, and weapons and gear were fully stocked.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year the armory was full again.

sentences.zh: 頻加中書侍郎、貞威將軍、黃門郎。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly given the posts of secretariat vice minister, steadfast-prestige general, and yellow-gate gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to secretariat vice minister, steadfast-prestige general, and yellow-gate gentleman.

sentences.zh: 十二年，吏部侍郎缺，所司屢舉王寬、謝燮等，帝並不用，乃中詔用引。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the vice ministry of personnel was vacant; the relevant offices repeatedly recommended Wang Kuan, Xie Xie, and others; the emperor used none of them and by personal edict appointed Yin.
translations.idiomatic: In year 12 the personnel vice ministry fell vacant. The offices kept recommending Wang Kuan and Xie Xie, but the emperor would not use them and by personal edict named Yin.

sentences.zh: 時廣州刺史馬靖甚得嶺表人心，而兵甲精練，每年深入俚洞，又數有戰功，朝野頗生異議。

translations.literal: At the time Ma Jing, inspector of Guangzhou, had won the hearts of the people beyond the ranges; his arms were drilled and keen; every year he penetrated deep into Liao caves; he also had repeated battle merit; court and countryside alike grew uneasy.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Jing, inspector of Guangzhou, then held great sway in the south. His troops were well trained, he raided deep into Liao territory every year, and he won battle after battle, so court and countryside alike grew uneasy.

sentences.zh: 高宗以引悉嶺外物情，且遣引觀靖，審其舉措，諷令送質。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan, because Yin knew conditions beyond the ranges thoroughly, also sent Yin to observe Jing, examine his conduct, and hint that he should send hostages.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan knew Yin understood the south and sent him to watch Ma Jing, judge his conduct, and urge him to send hostages to court.

sentences.zh: 引奉密旨南行，外託收督賧物。

translations.literal: Yin received the secret charge and went south, outwardly using collection and supervision of tribute goods as his pretext.
translations.idiomatic: Yin took the secret order south, publicly claiming to collect and oversee tribute goods.

sentences.zh: 既至番禺，靖即悟旨，盡遣兒弟下都為質。

translations.literal: When he reached Panyu, Jing at once grasped the intent and sent all his younger brothers down to the capital as hostages.
translations.idiomatic: At Panyu Jing saw through the mission at once and sent all his younger brothers to the capital as hostages.

sentences.zh: 還至灨水，而高宗崩，後主即位，轉引為中庶子，以疾去官。

translations.literal: On returning to the Gan River, Emperor Xuan died; Houzhu succeeded; Yin was transferred to junior mentor of the heir apparent and left office on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: On his way back at the Gan River, Emperor Xuan died and Houzhu took the throne. Yin was made junior mentor of the heir apparent but resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 明年，京師多盜，乃復起為貞威將軍、建康令。

translations.literal: The next year there were many thieves in the capital region; he was again raised as steadfast-prestige general and magistrate of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, with theft rife in the capital, he was recalled as steadfast-prestige general and magistrate of Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 時殿內

translations.literal: At the time, within the palace halls
translations.idiomatic: At the time, within the palace halls

translations.literal: (peng)
translations.idiomatic: (peng)

sentences.zh: 〔隊〕主吳璡，[14]及宦官李善度、蔡脫兒等多所請屬，引一皆不許。

translations.literal: [team] captain Wu Jin, [14] and the eunuchs Li Shandu, Cai Tuo'er, and others repeatedly pressed requests for favors; Yin refused every one.
translations.idiomatic: [team] captain Wu Jin [14] and the eunuchs Li Shandu and Cai Tuo'er pressed many private requests; Yin refused them all.

sentences.zh: 引族子密時為黃門郎，諫引曰：「李、蔡之勢，在位皆畏憚之，亦宜小為身計。

translations.literal: Yin's clansman Mi was then a yellow-gate gentleman; he remonstrated with Yin, saying: "Li and Cai's power—those in office all fear them; you too ought to make some allowance for yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Yin's kinsman Mi, then a yellow-gate gentleman, urged him: "Everyone in office fears Li and Cai. You ought to look out for yourself a little.

sentences.zh: 」引曰：「吾之立身，自有本末，亦安能為李、蔡改行。

translations.literal: " Yin said: "In establishing myself I have my own root and branch; how could I change my conduct for Li and Cai?
translations.idiomatic: " Yin said, "I have my own principles. How could I change my ways for Li and Cai?

sentences.zh: 就令不平，不過解職耳。

translations.literal: Even if it goes badly, at most I lose my post.
translations.idiomatic: If things go badly, I lose my post—that is all.

sentences.zh: 」吳璡竟作飛書，李、蔡證之，坐免官，卒於家，時年五十八。

translations.literal: " Wu Jin in the end composed an anonymous letter; Li and Cai bore witness; on this charge he was dismissed from office and died at home, aged fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Jin then sent an anonymous accusation, which Li and Cai backed. Yin was removed from office, died at home, and was fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 子德言，最知名。

translations.literal: His son Deyan was the most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: His son Deyan was the best known.

sentences.zh: 引宗族子弟，多以行義知名。

translations.literal: Among Yin's clansmen and younger kinsmen, many were known for righteous conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Many of Yin's clansmen were known for upright conduct.

sentences.zh: 弟彤，以恬靜好學，官至太子中庶子、南康王長史。

translations.literal: His younger brother Tong, through quiet ease and love of learning, reached the posts of junior mentor of the heir apparent and chief steward to the Prince of Nankang.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Tong, quiet and studious, rose to junior mentor of the heir apparent and chief steward to the prince of Nankang.

sentences.zh: 密字士機，幼而聰敏，博學有文詞。

translations.literal: Mi, styled Shiji, was clever and keen from childhood, broadly learned, and had literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: Mi, styled Shiji, was clever as a boy, widely read, and gifted in letters.

sentences.zh: 祖琛，梁特進。

translations.literal: His grandfather Chen was Liang special advance.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Chen had been Liang special advance.

sentences.zh: 父遊，少府卿。

translations.literal: His father You was director of the palace workshops.
translations.idiomatic: His father You was director of the palace workshops.

sentences.zh: 密太建八年，兼散騎常侍，聘于齊。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Taijian Mi was made acting attendant-in-ordinary and sent on embassy to Qi.
