translations.idiomatic: In Taijian year 8 Mi served as acting attendant-in-ordinary on embassy to Qi.

sentences.zh: 歷位黃門侍郎、太子中庶子、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of yellow-gate vice minister, junior mentor of the heir apparent, and attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He later held the posts of yellow-gate vice minister, junior mentor of the heir apparent, and attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：謝、王、張、蕭，咸以清淨為風，文雅流譽，雖更多難，終克成名。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Xie, Wang, Zhang, and Xiao all took purity and quiet as their wind; elegance and refinement flowed in reputation; though they met many hardships, in the end they achieved a name.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: Xie, Wang, Zhang, and Xiao all made purity their manner and won fame for culture. Though hardship followed them, they still made their names.

sentences.zh: 奐謇諤在公，英飆振俗，詳其行事，抑古之遺愛矣[15]。

translations.literal: Huan's blunt remonstrance in office and heroic wind that shook the vulgar—examining his conduct, he was indeed an ancient's lingering care left behind [15].
translations.idiomatic: Kong Huan's blunt honesty in office and heroic bearing that stirred the age show, on review, the lingering goodwill of the ancients [15].

sentences.zh: 固之蔬菲禪悅，[16]斯乃出俗者焉，猶且致絓於黜免，有懼於傾覆。

translations.literal: Gu's plain vegetables and Chan delight [16]—such men were beyond the vulgar; yet they still met entanglement in dismissal and fear of ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gu lived on plain food and Chan devotion [16], men above the common run, yet even they were snared in dismissal and feared collapse.

sentences.zh: 是知上官、博陸之權勢，閻、鄧、梁、竇之震動，吁可畏哉！

translations.literal: From this one knows the power of Shangguan and Bolu, the shock of Yan, Deng, Liang, and Dou—how dreadful!
translations.idiomatic: So one sees how fearsome were the powers of Shangguan and Bolu and the tremors of Yan, Deng, Liang, and Dou.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation notes

sentences.zh: 高祖為〔南〕徐州刺史 張森楷校勘記云：「案高祖紀，應作『南徐州刺史』。

translations.literal: The Founder as [south] inspector of Xuzhou—Zhang Senkai's collation note says: "According to the Founder's annals, it should read 'inspector of South Xuzhou.'
translations.idiomatic: On "the Founder as [south] inspector of Xuzhou": Zhang Senkai's collation note says the Founder's annals require "inspector of South Xuzhou."

sentences.zh: 」今據補。

translations.literal: " It is now supplied on that authority.
translations.idiomatic: South is now supplied on that authority.

sentences.zh: 昔陸賈南征趙他歸順 「趙他」各本作「趙佗」。

translations.literal: In old times Lu Jia on the southern campaign and Zhao Ta's submission—"Zhao Ta" in all editions reads "Zhao Tuo."
translations.idiomatic: On "Lu Jia's southern campaign and Zhao Ta's submission": all editions read Zhao Tuo.

sentences.zh: 今按佗他二字同音通用，趙佗之「佗」，論衡率性篇、譴告篇並作「他」。

translations.literal: Present examination: the graphs tuo and ta share sound and are used interchangeably; Zhao Tuo's "tuo" in the Lunheng chapters "On Nature" and "On Rebuke" both write "ta."
translations.idiomatic: Tuo and ta are homophones used interchangeably; Zhao Tuo's tuo appears as ta in the Lunheng chapters On Nature and On Rebuke.

sentences.zh: 二子儼

translations.literal: The two sons Yan
translations.idiomatic: On "the two sons Yan"

translations.idiomatic: (shen)

sentences.zh: 〔伷〕據南史改。

translations.literal: [zhou]—changed according to the History of the Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: [zhou]—emended per the History of the Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 按後主紀至德三年，以左民尚書謝伷為吏部尚書，「伷」亦訛「伸」，已據南監本改正。

translations.literal: According to the Houzhu annals, in the third year of Zhide, Xie Zhou of the left-household ministry was made minister of personnel—"zhou" is also written wrongly as "shen," already corrected on the authority of the Southern Supervisory edition.
translations.idiomatic: The Houzhu annals for Zhide year 3 name Xie Zhou of the left-household ministry as minister of personnel; zhou is also miswritten shen and is already corrected in the Southern Supervisory edition.

sentences.zh: 此則南監本亦訛，故據南史改。

translations.literal: Here the Southern Supervisory edition is also wrong; therefore it is changed according to the History of the Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Here the Southern Supervisory edition is also wrong, so the History of the Southern Dynasties is followed.

sentences.zh: 司徒王僧辯以狀

translations.literal: Minister of Education Wang Sengbian with a report
translations.idiomatic: On "Minister of Education Wang Sengbian with a report"

translations.idiomatic: (feng)

sentences.zh: 〔奏〕聞 據元龜四一三、七五四改。

translations.literal: [memorial] submitted and heard—changed according to Comprehensive Mirror 413 and 754.
translations.idiomatic: [memorial] submitted—emended per Comprehensive Mirror 413 and 754.

sentences.zh: 按南史作「以狀奏」，無「聞」字。

translations.literal: According to the History of the Southern Dynasties it reads "with a report submitted," without the character "heard."
translations.idiomatic: The History of the Southern Dynasties reads "with a report submitted," without heard.

sentences.zh: 又累賜無錫嘉興縣侯秩 御覽六四二引及元龜二〇九、三〇三皆無「侯」字，南史亦無「侯」字，「侯」字疑衍。

translations.literal: Also repeatedly granted the rank of marquis of Wuxi and Jiaxing counties—the Imperial Overview 642 citation and Comprehensive Mirror 209 and 303 all lack the character "marquis"; the History of the Southern Dynasties also lacks "marquis"; the character "marquis" is suspected as a spurious addition.
translations.idiomatic: On "also repeatedly granted the rank of marquis of Wuxi and Jiaxing counties": Imperial Overview 642 and Comprehensive Mirror 209 and 303 omit marquis, as does the History of the Southern Dynasties; marquis is probably a spurious addition.

sentences.zh: 齊護軍

translations.literal: Qi protector of the army
translations.idiomatic: On "Qi protector of the army"

translations.literal: (grandson)
translations.idiomatic: (grandson)

sentences.zh: 沖之〔孫〕按張沖南齊書有傳，稚才為其孫。

translations.literal: Chong's [grandson]—according to Zhang Chong's biography in the Book of Southern Qi, Zhicai was his grandson.
translations.idiomatic: On "Chong's [grandson]": Zhang Chong has a biography in the Book of Southern Qi; Zhicai was his grandson.

sentences.zh: 「孫」字應在「之」字下，各本並誤，今移正。

translations.literal: The character "grandson" should stand below the character "of"; all editions are alike in error; it is now moved to the correct place.
translations.idiomatic: Grandson should follow the particle zhi; all editions err; the word is now placed correctly.

sentences.zh: 太舟卿 南監本、汲本、殿本作「太府卿」，疑後人妄改。

translations.literal: Grand master of the great fleet—the Southern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions read "grand master of the great storehouse," suspected as a later man's reckless change.
translations.idiomatic: On "grand master of the great fleet": the Southern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions read grand master of the great storehouse, probably a later corruption.

sentences.zh: 參閱卷十六蔡景歷傳校記五。

translations.literal: See collation note five in the biography of Cai Jingli in scroll sixteen.
translations.idiomatic: See collation note 5 in the biography of Cai Jingli, scroll 16.

sentences.zh: 比將伏誅 南史作「比黨皆誅」。

translations.literal: About to be executed on the charge—the History of the Southern Dynasties reads "the whole faction was executed."
translations.idiomatic: On "about to be executed on the charge": the History of the Southern Dynasties reads "the whole faction was executed."

translations.literal: Xiao Yun, styled
translations.idiomatic: On "Xiao Yun, styled"

translations.idiomatic: (sheng)

sentences.zh: 〔叔〕佐 據北監本、汲本、殿本及南史改。

translations.literal: [uncle] Zuo—changed according to the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions and the History of the Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: [uncle] Zuo—emended per the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions and the History of the Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 尚書右僕射 按宋書蕭思話傳云「徵為尚書左僕射，固辭不受拜」，是思話未嘗為尚書右僕射也。

translations.literal: Right vice director of the masters of writing—according to the biography of Xiao Sihua in the Book of Song it says "summoned as left vice director of the masters of writing, firmly declined and did not accept investiture"—thus Sihua never was right vice director of the masters of writing.
translations.idiomatic: On "right vice director of the masters of writing": the Book of Song biography of Xiao Sihua says he was summoned as left vice director and firmly declined, so he never held the right post.

sentences.zh: 封陽穆公 按宋書蕭思話傳，思話襲爵封陽縣侯，卒謚穆。

translations.literal: Enfeoffed as Duke Mu of Yang—the biography of Xiao Sihua in the Book of Song shows Sihua inherited the rank and was enfeoffed as marquis of Yang county; on death his posthumous title was Mu.
translations.idiomatic: On "enfeoffed as Duke Mu of Yang": the Book of Song biography of Xiao Sihua shows he inherited and was enfeoffed marquis of Yang county; his posthumous title was Mu.

sentences.zh: 「公」當作「侯」。

translations.literal: "Duke" should read "marquis."
translations.idiomatic: Duke should read marquis.

sentences.zh: 天嘉三年徵為太子庶子 按下又云「三年，除稜威將軍丹陽尹丞」，兩「三年」字必有一訛。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianjia summoned as junior mentor of the heir apparent—below it again says "in the third year, made steadfast-prestige general and assistant magistrate of Danyang," so one of the two "third year" readings must be wrong.
translations.idiomatic: On "in Tianjia year 3 summoned as junior mentor of the heir apparent": below it again says "year 3, made steadfast-prestige general and assistant magistrate of Danyang," so one of the two year-3 notices must be wrong.

translations.idiomatic: (sheng)

translations.idiomatic: [uncle] Xiu—emended per the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions and the History of the Southern Dynasties.

translations.literal: At the time, within the palace halls
translations.idiomatic: At the time, within the palace halls

translations.literal: (peng)
translations.idiomatic: (peng)

translations.literal: [team] captain Wu Jin—changed according to the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions and the History of the Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: On "[team] captain Wu Jin": emended per the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions and the History of the Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 抑古之遺愛矣 張森楷校勘記云「遺愛」當作「遺直」。

translations.literal: He was indeed an ancient's lingering care left behind—Zhang Senkai's collation note says "lingering care" should read "upright legacy left behind."
translations.idiomatic: On "he was indeed an ancient's lingering care left behind": Zhang Senkai's collation note says lingering care should read upright legacy left behind.

sentences.zh: 今按張說是。

translations.literal: Present examination: Zhang's view is correct.
translations.idiomatic: On examination Zhang is right.

sentences.zh: 孔奐傳世祖云「古之遺直，復見於卿」，故史臣引之也。

translations.literal: Kong Huan's biography: Emperor Wen said, "The upright legacy of the ancients is seen again in you"—therefore the historiographer cited it.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Huan's biography records Emperor Wen saying, "The ancients' upright legacy appears again in you," which the historiographer echoed here.

sentences.zh: 固之蔬菲禪悅 「禪悅」各本作「蟬蛻」。

translations.literal: Gu's plain vegetables and Chan delight—"Chan delight" in all editions reads "cicada slough."
translations.idiomatic: On "Gu's plain vegetables and Chan delight": all editions read cicada slough.

sentences.zh: 按禪悅乃佛家語。

translations.literal: According to examination, Chan delight is Buddhist terminology.
translations.idiomatic: Chan delight is Buddhist language.

sentences.zh: 傳稱其崇信佛法，及丁所生母憂，遂終身蔬食，夜則坐禪，晝誦佛經。

translations.literal: The biography says he revered the Buddhist Law; when he completed mourning for his birth mother he thereafter for life ate only vegetables; at night he sat in Chan; by day he chanted Buddhist sutras.
translations.idiomatic: The biography says he devoutly followed Buddhism; after mourning for his birth mother he ate only vegetables for life, sat in meditation at night, and chanted sutras by day.

sentences.zh: 則作「禪悅」是。

translations.literal: Therefore to write "Chan delight" is correct.
translations.idiomatic: So Chan delight is correct.
